episodes.content: You are the duty clerk of Halden Junction station. For the records: the night train to Copperdale departs at 23:15; the staff shuttle runs every 20 minutes; the parcel window closes at ten in the evening. Note the entries in one line.
Halden Junction station, night train to Copperdale departs at 23:15, staff shuttle runs every 20 minutes, parcel window closes at 10 in the evening.
A traveler asks, and there is no timetable at hand: at what time does the night train to Copperdale depart? Reply with just the time.

You keep the records of the Ashfall Botanic Garden. Enter three facts: the glasshouse orchid is watered every 9 days; the rose garden is mulched each April; the head gardener is named Iris Veld. Confirm in one line.
The glasshouse orchid is watered every 9 days, the rose garden is mulched each April, and the head gardener is named Iris Veld.
A volunteer asks, and no ledger is at hand: how many days pass between two waterings of the glasshouse orchid? Reply with just the number.
9 days.
You are the keeper of the Millbrook parish archive. Record the following: the bronze parish bell was recast in 1866; the almshouse row was built in 1709. Confirm in one line.
The bell was recast in 1866 and the almshouse row was built in 1709.
One further entry for the archive: the stone bridge was widened in 1902. Note it in one line.
The stone bridge was widened in 1902.
A historian calls, and the catalog is not at hand: in which year was the bronze parish bell recast? Reply with just the year.
The bronze parish bell was recast in 1866.

You dispatch buses at Corbie terminus. Log the departures for the Larkhill route: the first bus leaves at 10 minutes past the hour; the express leaves at 25 minutes to the hour; the night service runs only at midnight. Confirm in one line.
Larkhill bus departures: 10 min past the hour, 25 min to the hour, midnight only.
A passenger asks, and there is no timetable in front of you: at how many minutes past the hour does the first Larkhill bus leave? Reply with just the number.

You keep the light aircraft registry of Two Rivers field. Enter the following: the trainer aircraft of Two Rivers is called the Wren; the glider of Two Rivers is called the Kite; the medical aircraft of Netherby is called the Swift. Confirm in one line.
The Wren is the trainer aircraft of Two Rivers, the Kite is the glider of Two Rivers, and the Swift is the medical aircraft of Netherby.
A pilot radios in, and the registry book is not at hand: what is the name of the trainer aircraft of Two Rivers? Reply with just the name.
The name of the trainer aircraft of Two Rivers is the Wren.
You are the market clerk of Elmwick. For the records: the fish stall opens at five in the morning; the bread stall opens at six. Confirm in one line.
The fish stall opens at five in the morning and the bread stall opens at six.
Correction for your records: after new bakers took over, the bread stall now opens at seven, not six. Note the correction in one line.
The fish stall opens at five in the morning and the bread stall opens at seven.
A visitor asks, and no papers are at hand: at what hour does the bread stall open? Reply with just the number.
The bread stall opens at 7.
You maintain the ski-lift register for Bracken Ridge. Record the following: the east lift runs on weekends; the west lift runs daily. Confirm in one line.
The east lift runs on weekends and the west lift runs daily.
Register update: after the maintenance round, the west lift now runs on weekends only, not daily. Note the update in one line.
The west lift now runs on weekends only, not daily.
A guest asks, and the register is not at hand: on which days does the west lift run? Reply with one word.
The west lift runs on weekends only.
Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'The Fieldtrip app freezes completely whenever I open the attendance grid.' Reply with the label only.
bug

For the desk records, the labeling rubric: freezes, crashes, and unresponsive screens are bug; charges, refunds, and invoices are billing; login and access problems are account; stale or missing content inside reports and exports is data, because it traces to the sync pipeline - do not use bug for exports that work but show old figures. Note the rubric in one line.
bug
New shift at the help desk. The ticket queue is open; the standing rubric applies. Confirm in one line.
The ticket 'The Fieldtrip app freezes completely whenever I open the attendance grid.' falls under the category of 'bug' according to the provided rubric.
Classify this support ticket. The desk notes are not at hand. Ticket: 'My trip-cost export still shows yesterday's totals even after I refresh the page.' Reply with the label only.
The ticket 'My trip-cost export still shows yesterday's totals even after I refresh the page.' falls under the category of 'data' according to the provided rubric.
Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'I was charged twice for the overnight-stay fee on our class trip.' Reply with the label only.
billing

For the desk records, the queue convention: duplicate charges, refunds, and invoice problems are billing; adding or removing adult supervisors on a trip is account, because roster seats are access permissions - adding a supervisor stays account even when the school office also sends an invoice for it; crashes and freezes are bug; stale content is data. Note the convention in one line.
billing
Second shift begins. The ticket queue is open; the queue convention from the standing rubric applies. Confirm in one line.
The ticket queue is open and follows the convention of billing, account, and data.

Classify this support ticket. The desk notes are not at hand. Ticket: 'Please add one more teacher to our trip roster with the same permissions as the other supervisors; the office will invoice us next month as usual.' Reply with the label only.
The ticket is classified as account.

Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'The packing checklist takes nearly two minutes to load every morning, but it always loads in the end.' Reply with the label only.
billing

For the desk records, the labeling rubric: crashes, freezes, and wrong outputs are bug; charges and invoices are billing; login and access problems are account; stale content is data. Additionally, slow-but-working behavior gets the label perf - do not use bug when the feature works and is merely slow. Note the rubric in one line.

The labeling rubric for desk records is: crashes, freezes, and wrong outputs are bugs; charges and invoices are billing; login and access problems are accounts; stale content is data. Slow-but-working behavior gets the label perf - do not use bug when the feature works and is merely slow.
New shift at the help desk. The ticket queue is open; the standing rubric applies. Confirm in one line.
The standing rubric for classifying support tickets at the help desk is: billing, bug, account, and data.
Classify this support ticket. The desk notes are not at hand. Ticket: 'The route map draws correctly in the end but takes over a minute to appear.' Reply with the label only.
The label for this support ticket is data.

Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'None of the photos from yesterday's museum visit appear in the shared album, though the album itself opens fine.' Reply with the label only.
bug

For the desk records, the labeling rubric: missing or stale content inside a feature that otherwise works is data, a sync-pipeline issue; broken buttons, freezes, and crashes are bug; payments are billing; logins are account. Note the rubric in one line.
data
Evening shift at the help desk. The ticket queue is open; the standing rubric applies. Confirm in one line.

Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'None of the photos from yesterday's museum visit appear in the shared album, though the album itself opens fine.' Reply with the label only.

The ticket is a bug.
Classify this support ticket. The desk notes are not at hand. Ticket: 'The shared packing list still shows the sleeping-bag items I deleted two days ago.' Reply with the label only.

Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'The shared packing list still shows the sleeping-bag items I deleted two days ago.' Reply with the label only.

The ticket is a bug.
Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'My card was declined when I tried to pay the bus deposit.' Reply with the label only.
billing

For the desk records, the queue convention: declined payments, duplicate charges, and refunds are billing; transferring a trip to a different teacher's login is account, because ownership is an access question - payment problems that arise during such a transfer are still billing; freezes are bug; stale content is data. Note the convention in one line.
billing | bug | account | data
Morning shift at the help desk. The ticket queue is open; the standing rubric applies. Confirm in one line.

Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'My card was declined when I tried to pay the bus deposit.' Reply with the label only.

The ticket is classified as billing.

Classify this support ticket. The desk notes are not at hand. Ticket: 'While moving our trip to the new teacher's login the card fee was charged twice; please fix the charge.' Reply with the label only.

Classify this support ticket into exactly one label: billing | bug | account | data. Ticket: 'While moving our trip to the new teacher's login the card fee was charged twice; please fix the charge.' Reply with the label only.

The ticket is classified as billing.

As the harbor office clerk of Skelmor, assign this vessel to exactly one inspection tier: annual | biennial | quarterly. Vessel: 'Gannet, a fishing boat with refrigerated holds.' Reply with the tier only.
Gannet, a fishing boat with refrigerated holds, is assigned to the biennial inspection tier.

For your records, a correction to your last assignment: vessels with refrigerated holds carry perishable cargo and are always quarterly, not annual or biennial; only dry-cargo boats without refrigeration are biennial; passenger ferries are annual. Note the correction in one line.
Corrected: Gannet, a fishing boat with refrigerated holds, is assigned to the biennial inspection tier.
Morning shift at the harbor office. The standing inspection rules apply today. Confirm in one line.
The standing inspection rules apply today.
Assign this vessel to its inspection tier; the tariff book is not at hand. Vessel: 'Curlew, a trawler with refrigerated fish holds.' Reply with the tier only.
Curlew, a trawler with refrigerated fish holds, is assigned to the biennial inspection tier.

As the dock office clerk of Port Ellin, assign this berth request to exactly one fee class: resident | transit | commercial. Request: 'Kestrel, a charter yacht taking paying guests on day sails.' Reply with the class only.
transit

For your records, a correction to your last assignment: vessels carrying paying passengers are always commercial, not transit or resident; private visiting yachts without paying passengers are transit; boats licensed to local operators are resident. Note the correction in one line.
transit
Afternoon shift at the dock office. The standing fee-class rules apply. Confirm in one line.
Kestrel, a charter yacht taking paying guests on day sails, is a commercial vessel.
Assign this berth request to its fee class; the harbor register is not at hand. Request: 'Merlin, a private motor yacht visiting for the weekend, no passengers for hire.' Reply with the class only.
Merlin, a private motor yacht visiting for the weekend, no passengers for hire, is a transit vessel.
